objective: Evaluate a design against the four principles and identify which are violated by common shortcuts (CI pushing to the cluster, hand-edited live resources, unversioned config stores)
secondaryObjectives: Pulled automatically: software agents pull the desired state from the source rather than having changes pushed to them, and why pull matters for security and reliability
Versioned and immutable: desired state stored in a way that enforces immutability and versioning with full history, and what that enables (audit, rollback, review)
Continuously reconciled: agents continuously observe actual state and attempt to apply the desired state, and the implications for manual changes and drift

The company, the clusters, the teams and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You chair the architecture review at Saltmarsh Bank, a fictional regional bank. The payments team calls its delivery flow GitOps and wants it approved as the bank's standard. You review it over three weekly design reviews.
handover: The flow: manifests in Git; CI runs kubectl apply with a cluster-admin token; on-call engineers hot-fix with kubectl edit; feature settings live in a key-value store edited in its web UI.
The bank's review board can approve a standard, approve it with conditions, or send it back.
howItWorks: The board shows the risk register against the appetite, each stakeholder's support in words and the docket.
Move on a week at a time. A decision comes to you at each design review; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

then.log: Week 2: a CI log leaks the cluster-admin token; for six hours it gives full control of every production cluster until it is revoked.
Week 3: a full deploy re-applies Git; three unrecorded hot-fixes are overwritten and the payments API fails for 50 minutes.
Week 4: someone sets a transfer limit to 0 in the UI; with no history, nobody can find the old value, and transfers fail for half a day.

effects.log: Week 1: the review starts with delivery.

pushPrompt.title: CI pushes with cluster-admin
pushPrompt.context: CI applies manifests with a cluster-admin token for every production cluster. No agent in the clusters pulls desired state.

choices.label: Require an in-cluster reconciler that pulls from Git; CI only builds, tests and updates Git; retire the cluster-admin token

effects.log: The condition is recorded: pull-based agents, no CI cluster credentials.

choices.feedback: Pulled automatically: agents in the cluster pull desired state, so no external system needs cluster credentials.

choices.label: Keep the push but scope CI's token to the payments namespaces
choices.feedback: Less blast radius, but it is still push: not GitOps, and nothing corrects drift.

choices.label: Approve the push model as GitOps: the manifests are in Git

effects.log: The push model is approved as the standard.

choices.feedback: Manifests in Git are not enough; a pushing CI with cluster-admin is the opposite of 'pulled automatically'.

editsPrompt.title: 62 resources drifted by hand edits
editsPrompt.context: On-call engineers hot-fix with kubectl edit; 62 resources now differ from Git, and nothing reconciles them.

choices.label: Hot-fixes go through Git (a fast-track pull request or a revert) and the reconciler corrects drift continuously; the 62 drifts are reviewed and either committed or reverted

effects.log: The condition is recorded: fixes via Git, drift corrected.

choices.feedback: Continuously reconciled: a manual change is drift, corrected back to the desired state; fixes are changes to that state.

choices.label: Allow kubectl edit with a ticket and backport to Git within a day

effects.log: Edits are allowed with a ticket and a backport.

choices.feedback: Better than nothing, but desired state lags reality, and a missed backport is undone at the next deploy.

choices.label: Turn reconciliation off in production so on-call hot-fixes stick
choices.feedback: Without reconciliation the drift grows; the next full deploy overwrites the unrecorded fixes.

storePrompt.title: Settings with no history
storePrompt.context: Fee and limit settings live in a key-value store edited in its web UI. It keeps no history and no review.

choices.label: Move the settings into Git as declarative config, reviewed by pull request and pulled by the reconciler, with the full history kept

effects.log: The condition is recorded: settings in Git, reviewed and versioned.

choices.feedback: Versioned and immutable: every change has a history, a reviewer and a way back.

choices.label: Export a nightly snapshot of the store to Git
choices.feedback: You get a daily record, but not who changed what, no review, and changes between snapshots are lost.

choices.label: Keep the store: business users need the web UI

effects.log: The store stays as it is.

choices.feedback: An unreviewed, unversioned change cannot be traced or rolled back.

reflection.question: Write the review decision: which principles the payments flow violated, and what the conditions require.

parts.label: Violations
parts.criteria: Push from CI (pulled automatically), hand edits with no reconciliation (continuously reconciled), and an unversioned store (versioned and immutable).
parts.modelAnswer: CI pushes with cluster-admin, which breaks 'pulled automatically'; hand edits drift with nothing reconciling; settings live in a store with no history.

parts.label: Conditions
parts.criteria: In-cluster agents pulling from Git, fixes through Git under continuous reconciliation, settings versioned in Git.
parts.modelAnswer: Agents pull from Git and CI loses its token; hot-fixes go through Git and drift is corrected; settings move to Git with review and history.

pushHarm.headline: Pull, don't push
pushHarm.body: GitOps agents pull from the source; no external system should hold cluster-admin to push changes.

editsHarm.headline: Drift is a defect

storeHarm.headline: Version the desired state
storeHarm.body: A versioned, immutable store gives history, review and rollback.

scoring.modelReasoning: GitOps has four principles: the desired state is declarative, versioned and immutable, pulled automatically by agents, and continuously reconciled. A CI job pushing with cluster credentials violates 'pulled automatically' and widens the attack surface; hand edits with no reconciler violate 'continuously reconciled'; a store without history violates 'versioned and immutable'. Storing manifests in Git does not by itself make a flow GitOps.
